objective: Ask whether combining the three live paper sleeves (S1 sector rotation, S2 growth rotation vol-targeted 0.156, S3 leveraged momentum vt40+dip boost 60/10) at a fixed monthly-rebalanced proportion earns a Sharpe and stress-period drawdown advantage over simply delevering S3 alone to the same realized volatility, using three preregistered weight rules (M1 equal-thirds, M2 half S1 half S3, M3 trailing-63-session inverse-volatility) each judged against its own volatility-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control, plus an M0 = S3-alone reference, while still clearing the frozen anchor-window G1/G1' bar at 10 and 20 bp.
target_regime_and_horizon: Common start 2017-02-01 (first session all three sleeves hold a non-cash position; S3 alone starts 2016-05-02, S1 2017-01-09, S2 2017-02-01, so 2017-02-01 binds). Stress period 2017-02-01..2023-09-15 (pre-select-window, includes the 2018 and 2022 drawdowns). Select window 2023-09-18..2025-12-31 (reported, not used to pick among M1-M3, since there is no ranking -- each candidate is judged against its own paired control). Anchor window 2024-01-08..2026-09-17 (frozen gate check, do-no-harm plus the transfer criteria). 2026-01-02..2026-09-17 holdout is reported but flagged contaminated: all three sleeves have already been evaluated on this window individually, so no fresh out-of-sample claim is made there. Validity is limited to the same US sector/growth-ETF and leveraged-ETF momentum regime the three sleeves themselves are limited to; this round does not claim the combination generalizes to other sleeve families or asset classes.
existing_solution_comparison: The general principle -- that a diversified (here, multi-sleeve) portfolio must be compared to a same-volatility levered-or-delevered version of the concentrated alternative, not to the concentrated portfolio at its own natural risk, or the 'diversification benefit' is just an artifact of lower average risk -- is Newfound Research's 'Portable Beta' analysis (2017-12-04, verified quote below) and is formally the same volatility/leverage-matching methodology AQR uses throughout its risk-parity papers (Understanding Risk Parity; Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity, Asness/Frazzini/Pedersen). No published source combines exactly S1/S2/S3 (our own frozen sleeves are proprietary parameter choices, not a published product), so there is no giant to replicate for the specific weight rules; what is reused is the comparison methodology (volatility matching) and, for M3, the well-established inverse-volatility weighting scheme used in risk-parity and trend-following overlay practice (Alpha Architect, Quantpedia). The registry dedup check (`oc research directions check sleeve combination diversification portfolio`, 2026-09-27) found no prior local test of combining our three sleeves; the closest hits (dir:meta_strategy_trailing_return_rotation -- rotating BETWEEN strategies by trailing return, not blending at a fixed or inverse-vol weight; dir:defense_first_taa_carlson_concretum -- a different asset-class tactical model) are a different mechanism.
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether S1/S2/S3's own daily returns are correlated enough that fixed-proportion or inverse-vol combination actually reduces stress-period drawdown versus just delevering the single highest-return sleeve (S3); this is exactly what has not been tested locally and is why the round reports pairwise sleeve correlation per window alongside the four preregistered pass conditions.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:meta_strategy_trailing_return_rotation (harvested, registry): rotating capital between strategies by trailing performance was found to lose to equal-weight -- a different mechanism (timing which strategy to hold) from this round's fixed-proportion or inverse-vol blending, but a reminder that naive combination rules do not automatically beat simpler ones. H-20260924-02 momentum daily crash guard (refuted, 0/5): an earlier attempt to de-risk S3 via a regime gate failed its adoption rule against an exposure-matched control -- the same EM/vol-matching control design this round reuses (as Ci) is why that refutation is trustworthy, and this round applies the identical discipline to the combination question.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Each sleeve's own daily net return already includes its internal 10bp (primary) or 20bp (stress) per-side turnover cost via scripts/run_h20260922_05_salvage.py's run_cell, unchanged. On top of that, the combination itself charges combo_cost_bps * sum(abs(delta weight)) on the session after each month-end rebalance signal (next-open fill, consistent with the frozen engine's convention). The Ci controls rebalance daily at their per-window fixed k with zero cost, which is conservative (favorable to the control, adverse to the combination).
stop_condition: If none of M1-M3 clears all four preregistered adoption-rule conditions against its paired control, the verdict is: fixed-proportion or inverse-vol combination of these three specific sleeves adds no measurable value over delevering S3 alone at the same risk, and the live-pilot decision should not adopt a combined-account structure on this evidence.

sources.claim: A levered/diversified 60/40 portfolio scaled to match the S&P 500's own volatility level outperformed the S&P 500 (12.5% vs 9.2% annualized in the modern period shown, at nearly identical ~14-15% volatility), illustrating that the value of diversification has to be judged against a volatility-matched (levered or delevered) version of the concentrated alternative, not against the concentrated portfolio at its own natural risk level.
sources.market_and_period: US 60/40 (S&P 500 / bonds) illustrative levered portfolio, 1962-2017 and a 'modern period' subsample shown in the post.
sources.applicability: Grounds the comparison methodology this round's C1-C3 controls implement: a diversified/combined portfolio's value must be judged against a volatility-matched version of the concentrated alternative (here, S3 alone), not against the concentrated portfolio's own unmatched risk level.
sources.limitations: Practitioner blog post illustrating 60/40 vs equities, not our specific ETF-rotation sleeves; no cost/tax treatment matching our contract.
sources.independent_replication: Same volatility/leverage-matching principle formalized in AQR's Understanding Risk Parity and Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity (Asness, Frazzini, Pedersen).

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Compute the three sleeves' pairwise daily-return correlations per window; if S1/S2/S3 are highly correlated (e.g. all > 0.85) in the stress period, combination is unlikely to beat a vol-matched control and the four-candidate screen (M1-M3 vs C1-C3) will show it directly via condition (c)/(d) without needing any further compute.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one of M1/M2/M3 clears all four preregistered adoption-rule conditions against its paired control in candidate-manifest.json.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: None of M1/M2/M3 beats its paired control's Sharpe by >=0.10 in both the anchor and stress windows, or none has a shallower stress-period drawdown than its control -- the combination adds no value over delevering S3 alone.
